issues.detail: The Hebrew clause 'יִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִים' (it goes down smoothly) is omitted in the Chinese translation. The Chinese ends with '流下順暢' which corresponds to 'יִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִים'? Actually, '流下順暢' is present, but the Hebrew has 'יִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִים' meaning 'it goes down smoothly' – the Chinese '流下順暢' captures that. However, the Hebrew also has 'כִּֽי יִתֵּ֣ן בכיס עֵינ֑וֹ' (when it gives its color in the cup) – the Chinese '在杯中閃爍' is a reasonable rendering. The issue is that the Chinese omits the initial 'אַל תֵּ֥רֶא יַיִן' (Do not look at wine) – but the Chinese has '不要看那變紅的酒' which includes that. Actually, the Chinese seems to cover all parts. Let me re-evaluate: The Hebrew has three clauses: (1) 'אַל תֵּ֥רֶא יַיִן' (Do not look at wine), (2) 'כִּ֪י יִתְאַ֫דָּ֥ם' (when it reddens), (3) 'כִּֽי יִתֵּ֣ן בכיס עֵינ֑וֹ' (when it gives its color in the cup), (4) 'יִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים' (it goes down smoothly). The Chinese: '不要看那變紅的酒' = Do not look at the reddening wine (covers 1 and 2), '在杯中閃爍' = sparkling in the cup (covers 3, though '閃爍' is not exactly 'gives its color' but acceptable), '流下順暢' = flows down smoothly (covers 4). So no omission. However, the Hebrew 'יִתְאַדָּם' is a verb meaning 'it reddens' – the Chinese '變紅' is correct. The issue might be that the Chinese adds '那' (that) which is fine. Actually, the translation seems complete. But wait – the Hebrew has 'כִּֽי יִתֵּ֣ן בכיס עֵינ֑וֹ' – 'when it gives its color in the cup' – the Chinese '在杯中閃爍' means 'sparkles in the cup' – that's a slight change but not a factual error. The main potential issue is that the Chinese says '流下順暢' which is fine. I think it's OK. But let me check if there's a negation issue – 'אַל תֵּרֶא' is 'do not look' – Chinese '不要看' is correct. So verdict should be OK. However, I flagged because I initially thought there was an omission, but re-reading, it's complete. Let me set verdict to OK.
